tldr: Headlines across all 12 national buckets frame the story through the SECURITY_DEFENSE register, reporting Israeli air strikes in West Bank's Jenin — described as killing 'terrorists' (Israeli, French, and wire-service outlets) or 'Palestinians' (Al Jazeera, Haaretz) — alongside concurrent strikes in Gaza. Israeli outlets split sharply: the Jerusalem Post leads with a named terror-cell operative eliminated after an intelligence effort; Haaretz leads on war crimes by Israeli-backed militias in Gaza. Pan-African and Italian outlets are alone in foregrounding humanitarian deterioration — Gaza shelter casualties and the West Bank's descent into a 'no-man's land.' Middle East Eye uniquely headlines Israel's defence minister declaring forces now 'occupy' the Jenin camp permanently.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to name the target by role ('Hamas-linked former senior Jenin terror cell member') and foreground the intelligence effort behind the strike — framing the killing as the conclusion of a counterterrorism investigation rather than a military event.

Only outlet to lead with Israeli culpability ('armed militias in Gaza to commit war crimes') — a self-critical Israeli headline that inverts the dominant security frame and is absent from every other national outlet.

Only outlet to headline Israel's defence minister declaring forces now permanently 'occupy' the Jenin camp — framing the military presence as territorial occupation rather than a temporary counterterrorism operation.

Only outlet to headline the kite-as-drone escalation story rather than the Jenin strike or Gaza casualties — a distinct military-threat sub-angle not present in any other national headline in this corpus.

bottom_line: Headline coverage frames this story overwhelmingly as a military-strike event; the sharpest cross-outlet divergence is in how the dead are named — 'terrorists' (Israeli military framing, echoed by French, wire-service, and Singapore headlines) vs. 'Palestinians' (Al Jazeera, Haaretz) — a labeling split that is invisible unless headlines are read comparatively across national buckets.
